findings.headline: Charts support a lower level than billed: 11 of 15 documented 99215s (73%), 14 of 43 charts overall
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 18.4% against 2.9% expected, and 42% of visits are for low-complexity patients. The random sample of 30 plus a targeted 99215 sample (43 usable charts; 7 targeted visits were not returned) gave a 33% below-billed rate. Peer rate is 0%. Note signals are low, so the notes do not look padded. They simply do not support the level billed. The random-sample overpayment estimate is NOT reliable because only 2 of the 30 random charts were 99215s. Do not quote a dollar figure.

findings.headline: 10 of 13 documented 99215s (77%) are below the billed level
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 18.1% against 2.0% expected, and 49% of visits are for low-complexity patients. The first response was a billing ledger. After follow-up, the random sample and a targeted 99215 sample gave 37 usable charts; 13 of them (35%) supported a lower level than billed. Peer rate is 0%. The overpayment estimate is NOT reliable because only 6 of the 30 random charts were 99215s. Do not quote a figure.

findings.headline: Concern rests on the notes, not the chart rule: 30% 99215 share on 1-condition patients, plus inflated-note and audit-trail signals
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 26.9% against 2.1% expected, and the panel is mostly low-complexity (0-1 conditions: 18-30% 99215 vs peer 1.5-2.7%). 24 of 30 random charts came back. The chart rule did not trigger, but 37.5% of notes address fewer problems than the billed level implies. The audit trail shows 25% of notes bulk-created, 12.5% paste-heavy and 25% signed late. Notes were first sent unsigned and later attested. This finding is weaker than a below-billed chart finding and needs a human coder to review the notes. The 6 visits that were never returned are not evidence.

findings.headline: High 99215 share on a healthy panel, but charts support the billed levels and audit-trail signals are low
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 21% against 1.7% expected, mostly on patients with 0-2 conditions. Across 50 charts (random plus targeted 99215), 0 supported a lower level than billed. 44% of notes address fewer problems than the claimed level implies, and the summary rule leaned toward upcoding. However, the audit trail showed little sign of padding: 8% bulk-created and 4% paste-heavy. Recommend a human coder review the problems-addressed examples (C0053442, C0053326, C0053444) before any leaning.

findings.headline: Very high 99215 share on low-complexity patients, but 49 charts show nothing billed above what the notes support
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 29% against 3.5% expected, and the share is high in every complexity band (13% even at 0 conditions). Across 49 charts, 0 were below billed. There are moderate note signals: 18-22% of notes describe data review that the claims' lab lines do not show, 33% are signed late, and 39% contain duplicate text. The audit trail showed only 4% bulk-created and 6% paste-heavy notes. The notes may be inflated to match the bill, but the evidence is not strong enough to lean either way. A human chart review is warranted.

findings.headline: Documentation supports billing, but the 99215 share is far above expected for a healthy panel
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 18% against 1.5% expected. Across 50 charts (random plus targeted), only 1 was below billed. 42-53% of notes address fewer problems than the claimed level implies, but there is no audit-trail evidence. Leave for human review.

findings.headline: 99215s cluster in patients with 5+ conditions; charts support billing
findings.interpretation: 98% of patients have more than minimal complexity, and 405 of the 518 99215s are for patients with 5+ conditions. The 99215 share in that group is above peers (42% vs 23%), but 30 random charts showed 0 below billed and almost no note signals. Largest dollar excess in the book, but the evidence points to a sick panel.

findings.headline: Moderately elevated 99215 share; charts mostly support billing
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 10% against 1.8% expected, on a large, mostly low-complexity panel. After a signature follow-up, 27 charts were usable: 1 was below billed, with low note signals. The random sample had too few 99215s to say more.

findings.headline: Elevated 99215 share; 2 of 30 random charts below billed
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 13% against 2.5% expected. Note signals are low. The random sample had too few 99215s to support a leaning.

findings.headline: Top claims outlier, but no records received
findings.interpretation: Highest risk-adjusted score: 32% 99215 against 1.7% expected, with 21-44% 99215 on patients with 0-2 conditions. The office asked for an extension and then did not respond to two follow-ups. Non-response is not evidence of upcoding. Still the strongest claims-only signal in the book; consider escalating the records request through provider relations.

findings.headline: Elevated 99215 share; office asked to clarify the scope, then did not respond
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is 23% against 3% expected, and it rises with complexity. No records were received. Non-response is not evidence.
